newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end choppy day mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end choppy day mixed.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended narrowly mixed after an erratic session spent struggling with a weak dollar and whipsawing Treasury bonds.
Stock index futures traders said there was little conviction on either side of the market Wednesday.
September Standard and Poor's 500 were firm with Treasury bonds on the open, encouraged by a batch of U.S. data that showed scant price pressure and as-expected retail sales.
But September failed to reach the 941.00 Globex high and technical weakness quickly set in. A T-bond and dollar rout exacerbated S&P's slide and shoved September as low as 916.00.
Stocks spent the rest of the day looking for direction. September S&Ps recovered slightly in afternoon trade, but cut gains once Treasury bond futures closed.
"I think sentiment has changed significantly in this market," an S&P 500 futures trader said. Gains seem more tentative and the mood more nervous than in recent months, he said.
An ongoing buy-the-dips mentality has kept losses in check, he said, but unless September S&Ps crawl back above 934.00, "that's technically pretty bad."
Traders put further support at 916.00 and 911.00.
Several traders said a good push lower could flush out any weak longs and set the market up for more new highs.
"Maybe we're taking a little bit of froth off the market," an S&P trader said.
Meanwhile, the focus was on Thursday data, including July consumer price index and industrial output and capacity use.

U.S. July producer price index fell 0.1 percent both overall and excluding food and energy, below the average forecast for a 0.1 percent gain in each index. U.S. July retail sales rose 0.6 percent overall and 0.5 percent excluding autos.
The average forecast had been for up 0.7 percent overall and up 0.5 percent ex-autos. Traders said the PPI showed no price pressures and retail sales were mostly in line with forecasts.

At the close, Sept S&P 500s were down 1.85 points to 925.80, KCBT Value Lines were 2.50 higher at 834.25, NYSE Composites were 0.50 lower at 480.35, Midcap 400s were 1.45 higher at 312.15, Nikkeis were 90 higher at 19,105, and Nasdaqs rose 7.50 points to 1105.25.
